steps.action: Mix two PDMS batches at offset ratios

steps.parameters: Pour batch A onto silanized SU-8 master to ~3 mm thickness. Bake 80 °C for 30 min on level hot plate (target 70-90% cure, surface tacky).

steps.parameters: Spin-coat batch B onto a silanized flat wafer at 1500-2000 rpm for 60 s (~50 µm thickness) or pour to 1 mm if used as cap. Bake 80 °C for 25 min.

steps.parameters: Peel layer A from master, punch fluidic vias with 0.75 mm biopsy punch, align onto layer B under stereo microscope. Apply gentle finger pressure or 50-100 g weight uniformly.
steps.notes: Misalignment >50 µm for valve geometries causes leakage; use registration marks.

steps.parameters: Bake stacked assembly 80 °C for 2-12 h (typical 4 h). Excess curing agent in B diffuses across interface and crosslinks with excess vinyl in A.

canonical_name: PMMA solvent welding via chloroform vapor
substrate_material: PMMA (poly(methyl methacrylate)) — cast and extruded grades both work
output_artifact: Optically clear monolithic PMMA chip with sealed channels; bond strength approaches bulk material.

steps.parameters: Use cast PMMA (e.g., Plexiglas G, Acrylite GP) 1-3 mm thick. Mill or laser-ablate channels in bottom half (50-500 µm wide). Drill access holes (1.5-2 mm) in top cap.
steps.notes: Cast PMMA bonds better than extruded (lower internal stress); extruded may craze. Channel surface roughness <5 µm Ra preferred for optical applications.

steps.parameters: Anneal both halves at 80 °C for 60 min in convection oven to relieve machining stress and reduce crazing.
steps.notes: Skip only if PMMA is freshly cast and unmachined; otherwise crazing risk is high.

steps.parameters: Wash with mild detergent (1% Liquinox in DI water) at 40 °C, sonicate 5 min, DI rinse, blow dry with N2 or filtered air. Dehydration bake 60 °C 15 min.
steps.notes: Avoid IPA or acetone soak (cracks PMMA); brief IPA wipe acceptable.

steps.parameters: Place PMMA halves face-up on perforated PTFE platform inside sealed glass chamber containing 5-10 mL chloroform in a Petri dish below. Expose 90-180 s at room temperature (22 °C).
steps.notes: Vapor swells the surface ~5-10 µm; over-exposure liquifies channels. Use minimum needed for tacky surface. CRITICAL: chloroform is a probable carcinogen; perform in fume hood with PPE.

steps.parameters: Immediately align top cap to bottom (use alignment pins or stereo microscope). Clamp uniformly at 0.5-1.5 MPa using flat aluminum plates. Hold at room temp 30-60 min, then transfer to oven.
steps.notes: Vapor-tackified surface bonds within seconds of contact; alignment must be done in <30 s after removal from chamber.

steps.parameters: Bake clamped assembly at 60-80 °C for 2-4 h to drive solvent evaporation and complete bond. Cool slowly under clamp.
steps.notes: Higher temp accelerates but risks channel collapse if PMMA softens (Tg ~105 °C); stay <85 °C.

Extruded PMMA often crazes at solvent exposure; visible white surface haze.
Skipped anneal causes crazing along machined edges within hours of solvent exposure.

equipment_required.notes: Must have PTFE or glass-only interior; many plastics dissolve in chloroform vapor.
Or simple bench clamp with flat aluminum plates.

steps.parameters: Expose bonding surfaces to UV/O3 (185+254 nm) at 10 mW/cm² for 5-15 min, OR brief O2 plasma 10 W for 30 s. This drops bond temperature by 5-10 °C.
steps.notes: Activation enables sub-Tg bonding at Tg-15 °C; without activation, bond at Tg-5 to Tg+5 °C.

steps.parameters: Place patterned COC half face-up, drop unpatterned cap on top. Align with pin features or registration marks. Place between fluoroelastomer pads (Viton) on aluminum platens.

steps.parameters: Press at 0.5-2.0 MPa, ramp to bond temperature at 5 °C/min, hold 5-15 min, cool to <Tg-30 °C under pressure. For Topas 5013: hold 125 °C (Tg-5 °C) at 1 MPa for 10 min. For 6013: 138 °C. For 8007: 73 °C.
steps.notes: Below Tg, bond is interdiffusion only; above Tg, channel deformation accelerates. Sweet spot is Tg-10 to Tg-2 °C with surface activation.

steps.parameters: Cool to room temperature at 2-5 °C/min under maintained pressure. Inspect bond zone with transmitted light for Newton's rings (unbonded areas appear as colored fringes).
steps.notes: Rapid cooling causes thermal-stress voids; slow ramp essential.

critical_parameters.target: Tg - 5 °C (with UV/O3 activation), or Tg + 0 to +5 °C (without)
critical_parameters.failure_at_off_spec: Below Tg-15 °C: insufficient interdiffusion. Above Tg+10 °C: channel collapse, loss of feature fidelity.
<0.3 MPa: voids and partial bond. >2.5 MPa: channel collapse, especially for shallow features.
<3 min: insufficient interdiffusion. >30 min: feature creep.
Mismatched grades distort asymmetrically; channels skew or close.

equipment_required.notes: Programmable temperature ramp essential; ±1 °C uniformity preferred.

equipment_required.instrument_class: hot embossing tool or CNC mill

validated_outcomes: Bond strength 5-15 N/cm peel (typical 8 N/cm at Tg-5 °C, 1 MPa, 10 min). Burst pressure 60-200 psi depending on channel width. Optical transparency >90% from 350-1000 nm. Autofluorescence ~1/10 of PMMA at 488 nm excitation. Channel deformation <5% with optimized parameters.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Colored interference fringes under transmitted light
failure_modes.corrective_action: Increase pressure or temperature by 2 °C; ensure platen flatness <10 µm.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Reduced or zero flow; visible channel width reduction under microscope
failure_modes.corrective_action: Lower bond temperature 3-5 °C; reduce pressure to 0.5 MPa; consider UV/O3 activation to enable lower temp.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Bond fails at chip perimeter under flow
failure_modes.corrective_action: Extend hold time to 15 min; verify edges clean and burr-free; consider local temperature gradients across platen.
Re-clean in HEPA-filtered environment; use anti-static wipes; pre-blow with ionized N2.
Reduce temperature (thermal degradation); check oven for organic contamination; ensure inert atmosphere if possible.

publication_citation: Mair DA, Geiger E, Pisano AP, Frechet JMJ, Svec F. Injection molded microfluidic chips featuring integrated interconnects. Lab Chip 2006; 6:1346-1354. DOI 10.1039/b605911b
sources: Topas COC application notes (TOPAS Advanced Polymers)
Roy et al. 2011 Sens Actuators B 161:1067 (UV/O3 activation for COC bonding)
notes: COC offers exceptional solvent resistance (vs PMMA), low autofluorescence, and high optical clarity to 250 nm UV. Preferred for fluorescence quantification, organic-solvent compatibility, and mass spec interfaces. Cost ~3x PMMA. Topas grade selection summary: 8007 for low-temp/elastic; 5013 for general; 6013 for stiff/high-temp.

canonical_name: COP (cyclic olefin polymer, Zeonex/Zeonor) thermal bonding
output_artifact: Optically clear, low-birefringence COP microfluidic chip with sealed channels.

steps.parameters: Pattern channels in Zeonor 1020R (Tg 102 °C, soft) or 1060R (Tg 100 °C, more rigid) via hot embossing or injection molding. Cap is unpatterned COP sheet.
steps.notes: Zeonex 690R (Tg 136 °C) has higher temp tolerance for thermal-cycle applications. COP has lower water absorption (<0.01%) than COC.

steps.parameters: Sonicate in 2% Hellmanex III 5 min, DI rinse 3x, IPA quick rinse (≤30 s), N2 dry, dehydration bake 70 °C 20 min.
steps.notes: COP is sensitive to prolonged alcohol exposure (surface stress cracking). Limit IPA to brief rinse.

steps.parameters: UV/O3 5-10 min OR low-power O2 plasma (10 W, 30 s). Lowers bond temp ~10 °C and enables sub-Tg bond.
steps.notes: COP is more responsive to UV/O3 than COC; activation effective for ~30 min before recovery.

steps.parameters: Place between PTFE pads on aluminum platens. Use alignment pins (~50 µm clearance) for multilayer chips.
steps.notes: COP is more transparent than COC at UV (good for transmitted-light alignment).

steps.parameters: For Zeonor 1020R (activated): 92 °C, 1.0 MPa, 10 min. For 1060R: 95 °C, 1.2 MPa, 10 min. For Zeonex 690R: 130 °C, 1.5 MPa, 12 min. Ramp 3 °C/min.
steps.notes: COP bonds slightly cleaner than COC at equivalent Tg-offset due to lower oligomer content.

steps.parameters: Cool 2 °C/min to <60 °C under pressure. Inspect for Newton's rings; pressure-test to design spec.
steps.notes: Rapid cooling causes birefringence and bond stress.

critical_parameters.failure_at_off_spec: Below Tg-15 °C: insufficient bond. Above Tg+5 °C: channel deformation.
<0.5 MPa: voids. >2.5 MPa: channel collapse.
<5 min: incomplete interdiffusion.
Mismatched Tg causes asymmetric warp.

equipment_required.notes: Optional but enables better channel preservation.
For pattern transfer if not injection molded.

validated_outcomes: Bond strength 7-12 N/cm peel. Burst pressure 80-180 psi for 100 µm channels. Optical transparency >91% from 350-1000 nm; transmits down to 200 nm with low absorption (better than COC). Birefringence <10 nm/cm with slow cooling. Yield 80-95%.

failure_modes.corrective_action: Slower cooling rate (≤1 °C/min); lower bond temperature; longer anneal.
Reduce bond temperature 3-5 °C; activate surfaces with UV/O3 to enable lower-temp bond; reduce pressure.
Anneal at 70 °C 30 min before bond; avoid IPA soak; verify no machining-induced stress concentrations.
Increase pressure 0.3 MPa; check platen flatness; extend hold time.

publication_citation: Steigert J, Haeberle S, Brenner T, Müller C, Steinert CP, Koltay P, et al. Rapid prototyping of microfluidic chips in COC. J Micromech Microeng 2007; 17:333-341. DOI 10.1088/0960-1317/17/2/020
sources: Roy et al. 2011 Sens Actuators B 161:1067
notes: COP differs from COC in monomer chemistry (single-monomer ring-opened vs ethylene-norbornene copolymer). COP has lower birefringence and water absorption — preferred for optics-heavy applications (interferometry, polarized fluorescence) and biological assays where dimensional stability matters. Higher cost (~5x PMMA) than COC.

canonical_name: Glass-glass low-temperature direct bonding via HF/H2O surface activation
substrate_material: Borosilicate glass (Borofloat 33, Pyrex 7740) or fused silica
output_artifact: Hermetically bonded glass-glass assembly with bond temperatures ≤400 °C (vs 600-650 °C for thermal fusion).

steps.parameters: Lap and polish bonding faces to <1 nm Ra (for direct bonding to work, surfaces must be smooth at atomic scale). Slides as supplied (Borofloat 33) typically meet this; verify with AFM.
steps.notes: Surface roughness >2 nm Ra prevents direct bond regardless of activation; this is the most common failure mode.

steps.parameters: RCA-1 (5:1:1 H2O:NH4OH:H2O2) at 70 °C for 10 min. Megasonic agitation if available. DI rinse, spin-dry or N2 blow.
steps.notes: Removes organic contamination and creates initial silanol surface. Substitute UV/O3 + dilute KOH if RCA-grade chemicals unavailable.

steps.parameters: Brief immersion in 0.5% HF in DI water for 60 s. Immediately DI rinse, then immerse in DI for 60 s. Spin dry or filtered N2.
steps.notes: HF removes native oxide and creates hydrophilic Si-OH surface. CRITICAL: HF is acutely toxic; full PPE and calcium gluconate available. Time strictly: longer etches surface.

steps.parameters: Bring activated surfaces into contact in clean (Class 1000 or filtered enclosure) environment. Apply gentle finger pressure at one edge to initiate bond wave (visible as advancing line).
steps.notes: Bond wave should propagate across full surface in <1 min. If it stalls, particle contamination is present — restart cleaning.

steps.parameters: Anneal bonded pair at 200-400 °C for 1-3 h in convection oven with slow ramp (2 °C/min). Optimal: 300 °C / 2 h.
steps.notes: Drives Si-OH + Si-OH → Si-O-Si + H2O; converts physisorbed bond to covalent. Higher temps give stronger bond but defeat low-temp purpose.

steps.parameters: Razor-blade test (insert thin blade at corner; bond should resist insertion past 1-2 mm). Look for IR Newton's rings to confirm full-area contact.
steps.notes: Razor test on test piece, not production chip.

critical_parameters.failure_at_off_spec: Bond fails to initiate; visible non-contact zones.
Higher: surface roughens; lower: insufficient activation.
>120 s: surface roughening; <30 s: incomplete activation.
<150 °C: bond remains physisorbed (van der Waals); easily separated. >450 °C: defeats low-temp purpose, may damage integrated thin films.
<30 min: incomplete dehydration; bond strength <20% of full.
Single ≥1 µm particle creates ~3 mm radius non-bonded zone.

equipment_required.notes: Mandatory for HF handling; PTFE bowls only.

validated_outcomes: Bond strength 1-2 J/m² surface energy after 200 °C anneal; 2-4 J/m² after 400 °C anneal (vs ~5-7 J/m² for full thermal fusion at 600+ °C). Hermetic seal verified by helium leak test (<1e-9 mbar·L/s). Bond yield over Class-1000 environment: 85-95%; bench-environment yield 30-60%.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: No bond wave propagation; surfaces remain separable
failure_modes.corrective_action: Re-verify surface roughness; re-clean with extended RCA-1 step; check for residual HF or water spots; reduce particle environment.
Improve cleanliness; check for trapped air bubbles by initiating bond from one edge slowly.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Cracking sound during ramp; visible separation
failure_modes.corrective_action: Slow ramp rate to 1 °C/min; ensure thermal-expansion match between substrates; check for trapped water (extend pre-bond drying).

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Hazy surface visible after HF dip
failure_modes.corrective_action: Reduce HF concentration to 0.3%; reduce time to 30 s; verify HF not contaminated with NH4F (which etches faster).

publication_citation: Plößl A, Kräuter G. Wafer direct bonding: tailoring adhesion between brittle materials. Mater Sci Eng R 1999; 25:1-88. DOI 10.1016/S0927-796X(98)00017-5
sources: Tong & Gösele 1999, Semiconductor Wafer Bonding (Wiley) — chapter on hydrophilic bonding
Howlader et al. 2010 Sens Actuators A 162:218 (HF activation for low-temp glass bond)
notes: Direct bonding sidesteps the 600-650 °C thermal fusion required for reagent-loaded or thin-film-integrated chips. The bond is hermetic but brittle; for cyclic-pressure applications anodic or thermal fusion remain stronger. Useful for sealing reagent reservoirs, low-temp packaging of optical sensors, or substrates with pre-deposited gold/platinum electrodes (which would melt or degrade at 600 °C).

canonical_name: Glass-glass anodic bonding via thin-film aluminum interlayer
substrate_material: Two borosilicate glass substrates (e.g., Borofloat 33 or Pyrex 7740) with sputtered aluminum interlayer on one face
output_artifact: Hermetically anodic-bonded glass-glass assembly at 200-350 °C using Al as Na-ion-mobilizing interlayer.

steps.parameters: On one glass substrate, sputter 100-300 nm Al at 100-300 W DC, 5 mTorr Ar, deposition rate ~5-10 nm/min. Pattern (lift-off or wet etch) to leave Al in bond zones only, leaving channels free of Al.
steps.notes: Channel zones must be Al-free to avoid metal contamination of fluid path. Al thickness 200 nm is typical compromise between coverage and stress.

steps.parameters: RCA-1 (5:1:1 DI:NH4OH:H2O2) at 70 °C 10 min, DI rinse, spin-dry. Final IPA wipe before bonding.
steps.notes: Skip oxygen plasma on Al surface (creates Al2O3 that blocks ion migration).

steps.parameters: Place Al-coated face against bare glass face. Use mechanical alignment pins (±50 µm).
steps.notes: Al-up or Al-down both work; many tools require Al-up for visual confirmation.

steps.parameters: Place stack on hot chuck, ramp to 200-350 °C (typical 300 °C). Apply -800 to -1500 V across stack with negative on bare glass side, positive on Al side. Hold 5-30 min until bond current decays to <10% of initial peak.
steps.notes: Bond current peaks then decays as Na+ ions migrate to cathode and depletion zone forms at Al/glass interface. Decay confirms bond completion.

steps.parameters: Maintain bias during cool to <100 °C, then ramp off voltage. Cool slowly (2 °C/min) to room temp.
steps.notes: Removing bias hot can allow Na+ back-migration; minor effect but degrades long-term bond.

steps.parameters: Visual: full-area bond visible as uniform contrast (vs Newton's rings for non-bond). Razor test on a sacrificial corner.
steps.notes: Bond strength similar to direct anodic bond; Al interlayer is consumed by oxidation in the process.

critical_parameters.failure_at_off_spec: <180 °C: insufficient Na+ mobility, weak bond. >400 °C: defeats low-temp purpose, Al may migrate.
<-500 V: insufficient field for Na+ migration. >-2000 V: dielectric breakdown of glass.
<50 nm: incomplete oxidation; bond non-uniform. >500 nm: stress-induced cracking on cool.
Watch bond current; insufficient time leaves un-bonded zones.
CTE mismatch causes thermal-stress cracks on cool.

equipment_required.notes: For Al deposition; e-beam evaporator also works.

equipment_required.instrument_class: anodic bonder or hot chuck + HV supply
equipment_required.optional_model: SUSS SB6 / EVG501 / DIY hot chuck + Glassman HV
equipment_required.notes: DIY: ceramic hot plate + electrically-isolated electrode + HV supply.

validated_outcomes: Bond strength 5-10 J/m² surface energy (comparable to silicon-glass anodic bond at higher temperature). Hermetic to <1e-9 mbar·L/s helium leak. Bond temperature 300 °C is 250-350 °C lower than direct fusion bonding. Yield 70-90% in published reports.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Constant high current >5 mA for >30 min
failure_modes.corrective_action: Check for arc-over (bias too high); verify Al continuity; confirm glass not too leaky.
Increase temperature 25 °C; verify Al planarity (lift-off can leave step heights >100 nm); add post-bond pressure if hot chuck supports it.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Visible metallic film inside channels post-bond
failure_modes.corrective_action: Verify Al patterning excluded channel zones; over-etch Al patterning; use lift-off rather than wet etch for finer control.
Verify CTE-matched glass pair; slow cool ramp to 1 °C/min; reduce Al thickness.

publication_citation: Berthold A, Nicola L, Sarro PM, Vellekoop MJ. Glass-to-glass anodic bonding with standard IC technology thin films as intermediate layers. Sens Actuators A 2000; 82:224-228. DOI 10.1016/S0924-4247(99)00376-3
sources: Wei et al. 2003 J Micromech Microeng 13:217 (low-temp glass anodic with Al)
Knowles & van Helvoort 2006 Int Mater Rev 51:273 (anodic bonding review)
notes: Standard glass-glass anodic bonding requires one substrate to be a Na-rich glass (Borofloat 33 has Na2O ~4 wt%). Bonding two pieces of the same glass type was traditionally limited; the Al interlayer enables anodic bonding by providing the cathode interface for Na+ ion migration without needing a silicon substrate. The Al is consumed (oxidized to Al2O3 in the depletion zone). Useful for fully-glass MEMS packages and chips with delicate pre-deposited features.

canonical_name: Thermoplastic-to-glass UV adhesive bonding with Norland NOA-86
substrate_material: Thermoplastic chip (PMMA, COC, or COP) plus glass substrate; NOA-86 UV-cure adhesive interlayer
output_artifact: Thermoplastic-glass hybrid chip with optically clear bond, suitable for inverted microscopy of plastic-based assays.

steps.parameters: Glass: 2% Hellmanex sonication 5 min, DI rinse, IPA, N2 dry. Thermoplastic: water + IPA wipe (avoid solvents that craze the plastic). Both: dehydrate at 60 °C 15 min.
steps.notes: Use lint-free wipes; particulate causes localized non-bond.

steps.parameters: Spin-coat NOA-86H or NOA-86 at 3000-5000 rpm 30 s for 2-5 µm thickness, OR pipette ~5 µL per cm² for capillary-fill assembly. Degas adhesive in vacuum desiccator 5 min before use.
steps.notes: NOA-86 is solvent-thinned (vs NOA-81 which is solvent-free); spin-coats more easily.

steps.parameters: Place thermoplastic chip face-down onto adhesive-coated glass. Press with finger or 100 g weight. Allow capillary action to spread adhesive into bond zone.
steps.notes: For sealed channels: ensure adhesive does not bleed into channels (use channel chip face-up with cap chip, or pre-coat only bond rails).

steps.parameters: For NOA-86 (solvent-containing): hold at 60 °C 5 min on hot plate with chip un-clamped to flash solvent before UV cure. Skip for NOA-86H (solvent-free variant).
steps.notes: Trapped solvent causes bubbles during UV cure.

steps.parameters: Expose 365 nm UV at 10-30 mW/cm² for 60-180 s (total dose 1-5 J/cm²). UV must transmit through glass side (NOA cures via UV).
steps.notes: NOA cure dose (Norland datasheet): 1.5 J/cm² minimum for full cure. For 5 µm bond layer, 2 J/cm² recommended.

steps.parameters: Bake at 50-80 °C for 12-24 h to drive secondary thermal cure and increase modulus. Optional but recommended for chemical resistance.
steps.notes: Increases bond strength ~30%; enables IPA, ethanol, weak acid use in channels.

critical_parameters.failure_at_off_spec: <1 µm: starvation, bond gaps. >20 µm: shrinkage stress, channel deformation, optical aberration.
<1 J/cm²: under-cure, soft bond, leaches uncured monomer. >5 J/cm²: yellowing, embrittlement.
Skipped flash: trapped solvent bubbles after cure.
Both surfaces opaque to UV: cannot cure. Use UV-transparent thermoplastic (PMMA, COP) and cure through plastic if glass is metallized.

equipment_required.optional_model: Omnicure S2000 / Lumen Dynamics / 365 nm LED panel
equipment_required.notes: 365 nm peak; 405 nm also cures NOA-86 but slower.
For thin uniform adhesive layer; otherwise use pipette + capillary spread.
For solvent flash and post-cure thermal.

materials_required.material: Norland Optical Adhesive NOA-86 or NOA-86H

validated_outcomes: Bond strength 5-15 N/cm peel (varies with substrate; PMMA-glass typically 8-12 N/cm). Burst pressure 30-100 psi for 100 µm channels. Optical transmittance >92% from 400-1000 nm. NOA-86 cured: refractive index 1.46 (close to glass), minimal optical aberration. Chemical resistance: stable in water, dilute saline; degrades in DMSO, dichloromethane, strong bases.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Channel cross-section reduced; visible meniscus at channel walls
failure_modes.corrective_action: Reduce adhesive volume; use selective coating (only on bond rails, not channel zones); consider stencil-printing adhesive.
Better solvent flash (extend to 10 min); degas adhesive longer; use NOA-86H solvent-free variant.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Bond layer turns yellow over weeks
failure_modes.corrective_action: Limit UV overdose; some yellowing intrinsic to NOA family in storage; consider NOA-63 for less yellowing if bond strength permits.
Reduce adhesive thickness; reduce shrinkage by post-cure thermal treatment after partial UV cure rather than full UV cure.
Verify chemical compatibility (NOA-86 datasheet); consider NOA-72 (more solvent-resistant) or NOA-88 (high-T variant).

publication_citation: Sollier E, Murray C, Maoddi P, Di Carlo D. Rapid prototyping polymers for microfluidic devices and high pressure injections. Lab Chip 2011; 11:3752-3765. DOI 10.1039/c1lc20514e
sources: Bartolo et al. 2008 Lab Chip 8:274 (NOA microfluidic chips)
Wagli et al. 2011 Anal Chem 83:7558 (NOA-81 vs NOA-86 comparison)
notes: NOA family ranking by hardness/Tg: NOA-63 (soft, bondable) < NOA-81 (medium) < NOA-86 (harder, more solvent-resistant) < NOA-88 (high-temp). For thermoplastic-glass bonding, NOA-86 is the best general-purpose choice. NOA bonds are reversible at >150 °C — useful for chip recycling but limits high-temp PCR applications.

canonical_name: Hydrogel-PDMS bonding via PEGDA covalent attachment
substrate_material: PDMS chip + PEGDA hydrogel layer (Mn 575 to 6000)
output_artifact: Hybrid PDMS-hydrogel chip with chemically bonded interface; suitable for cell-laden hydrogel chambers, drug-release studies, ECM-mimetic tissue chips.

steps.parameters: O2 plasma activate PDMS (18 W, 30 s). Immediately immerse in 5% (v/v) (3-mercaptopropyl)trimethoxysilane (MPTMS) in dry toluene for 60 min at room temp. Rinse in toluene, IPA, N2 dry, cure 80 °C 60 min.
steps.notes: Plasma → silanol → silanized within 5 min ensures Si-O-Si-(CH2)3-SH terminus. MPTMS handle in fume hood (sulfur odor).

steps.parameters: Mix PEGDA (Mn 575 for stiff, 4000-6000 for soft hydrogel) at 20-50% w/v in PBS or DI. Add 0.5-1.0% w/v photoinitiator: Irgacure 2959 (UV, biocompatible) or LAP (visible light, biocompatible). Filter 0.22 µm, degas under vacuum 5 min.
steps.notes: PEGDA Mn 575 yields G' ~50-200 kPa; Mn 6000 yields G' ~0.5-5 kPa. Tune for cell-type stiffness sensitivity.

steps.action: Inject PEGDA into thiolated PDMS channel
steps.parameters: Pipette PEGDA solution into channel via inlet port; ensure no air bubbles. Cap inlet/outlet to prevent evaporation.
steps.notes: For partial-filling (gel only in defined region), use laminar-flow patterning or photomask.

steps.parameters: Expose 365 nm UV at 10-20 mW/cm² for 30-120 s (dose 0.3-2 J/cm²). The diacrylate end groups undergo radical polymerization, while thiol on PDMS surface participates in thiol-acrylate Michael / radical addition, covalently linking gel to PDMS.
steps.notes: Lower doses (0.3 J/cm²) preserve cell viability if cells encapsulated. LAP allows visible-light cure (405 nm) for cell viability.

steps.parameters: Flush channel with PBS for 10 column volumes to remove uncrosslinked PEGDA and initiator residue. Equilibrate at 37 °C in cell media if used for culture.
steps.notes: Uncrosslinked PEGDA is mildly cytotoxic; thorough wash essential.

steps.parameters: Pressure test: ramp inlet pressure to 5-10 psi, observe gel for delamination or extrusion through interface. For cell chambers, simply confirm gel doesn't slide under flow.
steps.notes: Bond is weaker than PDMS-glass plasma bond but sufficient for cell-handling pressures.

critical_parameters.failure_at_off_spec: Skipped: hydrogel slides off PDMS under flow. Wet toluene: silane hydrolyzes in solution.
<15%: gel doesn't form continuous network. >60%: high osmotic stress on cells.
<0.2%: incomplete cure. >2%: cytotoxicity for cell-laden formulations.
Low dose: under-crosslinked gel. High dose: cell death; brittle gel.
Surface silanols recover hydrophobicity within minutes; delayed silanation reduces grafting density.

validated_outcomes: Hydrogel-PDMS interface adhesion strength 5-30 kPa shear (depends on MPTMS density and PEGDA Mn). Hydrogel modulus tunable 0.5 kPa - 200 kPa. Cell viability (3T3, HUVEC, primary hepatocytes) >85% with LAP at 0.5% / 1 J/cm² visible light. Hydrogel withstands flow shear up to 5 dyn/cm² without delamination.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Gel slides as a plug under flow
failure_modes.corrective_action: Verify MPTMS treatment fresh; extend silane time to 90 min; verify plasma activation immediately preceded silane; consider CGRGDS peptide co-tethering for additional anchoring.
Better degassing of PEGDA precursor; slower channel filling; vacuum-assisted filling.
Reduce UV dose or switch to LAP/visible light; reduce photoinitiator concentration; reduce PEGDA concentration (osmotic stress).
Match osmolarity of crosslinking buffer to use buffer; allow equilibration time before measurement.
Use stiffer hydrogel formulation (lower Mn PEGDA); increase channel aspect ratio; consider rigid posts as gel-confinement structures.

publication_citation: Cha C, Su WT, Wang HF, et al. Microfluidically generated cell-laden hydrogel microspheres for tissue engineering applications. Biomicrofluidics 2012; 6:024118. DOI 10.1063/1.4724460
sources: DeForest & Anseth 2012 Annu Rev Chem Biomol Eng 3:421 (PEGDA + thiol-ene chemistry)
Hoffmann et al. 2008 Lab Chip 8:935 (PEGDA-PDMS bonding)
notes: Thiol-ene click chemistry between MPTMS-functionalized PDMS and PEGDA's vinyl groups gives covalent grafting without cytotoxic catalysts. For cell-laden hydrogels, LAP + visible 405 nm light dramatically improves viability vs. Irgacure 2959 + 365 nm. GelMA, GelDA, and HAMA hydrogels can substitute for PEGDA with similar thiol-ene grafting chemistry.

canonical_name: BSA (bovine serum albumin) surface passivation for PDMS channels
substrate_material: Assembled PDMS-glass microfluidic chip (any soft-litho geometry)
output_artifact: PDMS chip with BSA-blocked surfaces; reduces non-specific protein adsorption and cell attachment for short-term assays.

steps.parameters: Flush channel with 70% ethanol for 5 min, then PBS (1x) for 10 min, both at 5 µL/min via syringe pump.
steps.notes: Ethanol wets hydrophobic PDMS and removes uncured oligomers. Skip ethanol if cells already in chip.

steps.parameters: Flush 1-5% (w/v) BSA in PBS through channel at 1-5 µL/min for 10 min. Use Fraction V or higher purity BSA. Pre-filter 0.22 µm to remove aggregates.
steps.notes: BSA Cohn fraction V is standard; for fluorescence-critical work use BSA pre-tested for low autofluorescence.

steps.parameters: Stop flow, incubate at room temp 30 min to 2 h, OR at 4 °C overnight for higher passivation density.
steps.notes: 4 °C overnight gives most uniform monolayer; room temp 30 min is sufficient for short assays.

steps.parameters: Flush 5 column volumes of PBS at 5-10 µL/min. Or 0.05% Tween-20 in PBS if downstream assay requires.
steps.notes: Insufficient wash leaves loose BSA that competes with assay reagents.

steps.parameters: BSA layer is stable for 4-24 h at 4 °C in PBS. For longer storage, exchange to PBS + 0.02% sodium azide at 4 °C for up to 1 week.
steps.notes: BSA passivation degrades over days; re-passivate before reuse.

critical_parameters.failure_at_off_spec: <0.5%: incomplete coverage. >10%: aggregation, channel clogging.
<10 min: sub-monolayer coverage.

critical_parameters.target: Fraction V, fatty-acid-free for sensitive assays
critical_parameters.failure_at_off_spec: Lower-purity BSA (e.g., Fraction II/III) introduces lipid and immunoglobulin contaminants that bias non-specific adsorption.

critical_parameters.target: PBS or DI, free of detergent
critical_parameters.failure_at_off_spec: Residual detergent (Tween, Triton) competes with BSA for surface.

validated_outcomes: Reduces non-specific protein adsorption to PDMS by 60-90% (fluorescent-protein adsorption assays). Reduces cell adhesion to PDMS by 70-95% over 24 h (NIH-3T3, HEK293). Surface stable 4-24 h. Compatible with most aqueous buffers but disrupted by SDS, urea, organic solvents.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Visible air gap; non-uniform BSA coverage
failure_modes.corrective_action: Pre-wet channel with 70% ethanol then PBS; inject BSA slowly with channel inclined to vent bubbles.
Filter BSA solution 0.22 µm; do not vortex BSA; gentle inversion mixing only.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Cells attach and spread on PDMS surface despite BSA
failure_modes.corrective_action: Extend BSA incubation to overnight 4 °C; verify no detergent residue from cleaning; consider Pluronic F-127 (often more durable for cell-adhesion blocking) or PEG-silane.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Non-specific binding returns within hours of use
failure_modes.corrective_action: Increase BSA concentration; use BSA in physiological buffer (not pure water, which can desorb BSA); avoid high shear flow.
Use higher-purity BSA (fatty-acid-free); switch to casein or Pluronic for fluorescence-sensitive assays.

publication_citation: Wong I, Ho CM. Surface molecular property modifications for poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) based microfluidic devices. Microfluid Nanofluid 2009; 7:291-306. DOI 10.1007/s10404-009-0443-4
notes: BSA passivation is the simplest and lowest-cost PDMS blocking strategy. Limitations: short-lived (hours), sensitive to surfactants, not suitable for chips run weeks at a time. For longer-term passivation use Pluronic F-127 (adsorbed PEO chains), PEG-silane (covalent), or PEGylation. BSA is also incompatible with assays where albumin binds the analyte (e.g., free-fatty-acid assays) — use casein blocker as substitute.

canonical_name: PEG-silane covalent anti-fouling coating for PDMS / glass channels
output_artifact: Covalently grafted PEG monolayer reducing non-specific protein and cell adhesion for weeks-long stability.

steps.parameters: O2 plasma at 18-50 W, 30-60 s, with sealed chip (gas-flow port active). Generates Si-OH groups on both PDMS and glass.
steps.notes: For sealed chips, alternative is in-situ NaOH activation (1 M NaOH flow 30 min). Plasma is more reproducible.

steps.parameters: Mix 5% (v/v) 2-[methoxy(polyethyleneoxy)6-9propyl]-trimethoxysilane (mPEG-silane, MW ~460-590) in 95:5 ethanol:water with 0.1% acetic acid (for hydrolysis catalysis). Flow through channel 5 µL/min for 10 min.
steps.notes: Higher MW PEG-silanes (PEG2000-silane, PEG5000-silane) give thicker brush layers but slower diffusion into channels.

steps.parameters: Stop flow, incubate at room temp 30 min to 2 h. Higher temperature (40 °C) accelerates condensation but evaporates ethanol — use sealed chip.
steps.notes: Time-density tradeoff: 30 min gives sub-monolayer; 2 h approaches monolayer.

steps.parameters: Drain channel, then bake chip at 60-90 °C for 30-60 min in convection oven or hot plate. Drives Si-O-Si covalent bond formation.
steps.notes: Higher temp gives denser brush but risks PDMS shrinkage / channel deformation > 100 °C.

steps.parameters: Flush channel: ethanol 5 column volumes, DI 5 column volumes, PBS 5 column volumes.
steps.notes: Removes physisorbed silane and hydrolysis byproducts.

steps.parameters: Optional: contact angle measurement (PEG-coated PDMS ≤ 30° vs ~110° for native PDMS). Or fluorescent BSA adsorption assay (>90% reduction expected).
steps.notes: Static vs sliding contact angle distinguishes uniform monolayer from patchy coating.

critical_parameters.failure_at_off_spec: <1%: sub-monolayer coverage. >15%: aggregates and crosslinking in solution rather than on surface.
No catalyst: very slow grafting; >1% acid: solution polymerization.
PDMS hydrophobic recovery: surface returns to native hydrophobicity within minutes; silanols recombine.
<40 °C: bond not fully covalent; eventually washes off. >100 °C: PDMS shrinkage and channel deformation.
Wrong MW for application: short PEG insufficient for protein blocking; long PEG can clog narrow channels.

validated_outcomes: Static contact angle on PDMS reduced from ~110° to 25-40°. Non-specific BSA-FITC adsorption reduced 90-99%. Cell adhesion blocked for 1-4 weeks (vs hours for BSA passivation). Compatible with detergents, mild acids and bases. Surface stable in PBS + 0.02% azide at 4 °C for >30 days.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Contact angle returns to native values within hours
failure_modes.corrective_action: Verify cure step (heat); extend cure to 90 min; verify plasma activation immediately preceded silane (not delayed).
Use shorter PEG (MW <1000); use lower silane concentration; flush with extra ethanol after grafting to remove crosslinked silane aggregates.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Inhomogeneous contact angle / fluorescent BSA shows hot-spot adsorption
failure_modes.corrective_action: Higher silane concentration; longer incubation; confirm plasma uniformity across chip.
Reduce cure temperature to 60 °C / longer time; or use UV cure (NOA-style) PEG instead of thermal cure.

publication_citation: Sharma V, Dhayal M, Govind, Shivaprasad SM, Jain SC. Surface characterization of plasma-treated and PEG-grafted PDMS for micro fluidic applications. Vacuum 2007; 81:1094-1100. DOI 10.1016/j.vacuum.2006.12.008
sources: Papra et al. 2001 Langmuir 17:1457 (PEG-silane SAM on glass)
Lee et al. 2005 Langmuir 21:11957 (PEG-silane on PDMS)
notes: Most durable benchtop PDMS antifouling option not requiring polymerization chemistry. Limitations: silane chemistry sensitive to water content in solution; ethanol-water ratio matters. For very long-term (>1 month) stability, combine with weekly re-flush to refresh PEG layer.

canonical_name: Silane SAM library: APTES, OTS, MPTMS, fluorosilane workflows
substrate_material: Silicon, glass, or PDMS surfaces (post O2 plasma)
output_artifact: Self-assembled monolayer with engineered surface chemistry: amine (APTES) for biofunctionalization, methyl (OTS) for hydrophobic, thiol (MPTMS) for thiol-ene grafting, fluoroalkyl for super-hydrophobic / mold-release.

steps.parameters: O2 plasma 18-50 W for 30-60 s. Or for glass: piranha 4:1 H2SO4:H2O2 5 min, DI rinse. Generates surface silanol density ~5/nm².
steps.notes: All silane SAMs require silanol surface as anchor. Hydrophobic recovery starts within minutes — proceed immediately.

steps.parameters: For each silane: dissolve 2-5% v/v in dry anhydrous toluene (alkyl silanes: OTS, fluorosilane) or 95:5 EtOH:H2O with 0.1% acetic acid (amino silanes: APTES; thiol silanes: MPTMS). Immerse substrate 30-60 min RT, agitate gently.
steps.notes: OTS/fluorosilane: water content in toluene must be <50 ppm or you get polymer aggregates instead of SAM. APTES tolerates 5% water (helps hydrolysis).

steps.action: Vapor-phase silanation (Method B — for fluorosilane mold release)
steps.parameters: Place substrate in sealed vacuum desiccator with 50-200 µL silane in open vial. Pump down to <1 Torr, hold 1-12 h at room temp.
steps.notes: Vapor-phase preferred for fluorosilane (controls thickness; avoids solvent residue). For trichloro(perfluorooctyl)silane, 1 h is sufficient.

steps.parameters: Method A: rinse in fresh solvent (toluene or EtOH) 3 x 30 s, then orthogonal solvent (IPA or H2O), N2 dry. Method B: no rinse needed; vacuum exposure removes excess.
steps.notes: Insufficient rinse leaves multilayer on top of SAM.

steps.parameters: For amine, thiol, alkyl silanes: 80-110 °C for 30-60 min in convection oven. For fluorosilane (vapor): no bake needed (vapor phase + vacuum gives covalent grafting). Drives Si-O-Si bond formation.
steps.notes: Higher cure temperature gives denser SAM; >130 °C may degrade amine groups.

steps.parameters: Static water contact angle measurement: APTES ≅50-65°; OTS ≅100-110°; MPTMS ≅65-75°; fluorosilane ≅110-120°. Or XPS for elemental confirmation if available.
steps.notes: Out-of-spec contact angle indicates patchy or sub-monolayer coverage.

critical_parameters.failure_at_off_spec: Wrong functional group for downstream chemistry.
OTS / fluorosilane polymerize in solution and deposit aggregates instead of SAM.
<0.5%: sub-monolayer. >10%: aggregates.
Hydrophobic recovery on PDMS reduces silanol density; on glass slower (~30 min) but still degrades.
Below: physisorbed only; washes off. Above 130 °C: amine degradation; PDMS shrinkage.

equipment_required.notes: All silanes require fume hood; many are toxic or moisture-sensitive.
For vapor-phase silanation; pump to <1 Torr.

equipment_required.optional_model: Ramé-Hart / DataPhysics OCA / DIY USB camera

validated_outcomes: APTES on glass: -NH2 density ~3-5 groups/nm², contact angle 50-65°, suitable for protein conjugation via NHS-ester chemistry. OTS on glass: contact angle 105-110°, suitable for hydrophobic surface patterning. MPTMS on glass: -SH density ~2-4 groups/nm², suitable for thiol-ene grafting of acrylates. Fluorosilane on Si master: contact angle 115-120°, mold-release > 100 PDMS releases without master degradation.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: AFM/SEM shows particles or films; non-uniform contact angle
failure_modes.corrective_action: Use anhydrous solvent; reduce silane concentration; reduce immersion time; verify silane bottle not aged (water ingress over months).

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Contact angle returns to native within hours
failure_modes.corrective_action: Increase cure temperature; verify activation immediately preceded silanation; check substrate cleanliness.
Improve activation uniformity (rotate substrate in plasma); ensure complete substrate immersion; longer incubation.
Use fresher APTES (degrades over months); reduce cure temperature to <100 °C; reduce APTES concentration to 1%.
Re-silanize with fresh fluorosilane; increase vapor exposure to overnight; verify master surface clean before silanation.

publication_citation: Sagiv J. Organized monolayers by adsorption. 1. Formation and structure of oleophobic mixed monolayers on solid surfaces. J Am Chem Soc 1980; 102:92-98. DOI 10.1021/ja00521a016
sources: Gelest Silane Coupling Agents handbook (free, comprehensive)
Lee et al. 1989 Anal Chem 61:935 (silane SAM characterization)
notes: Reference cookbook for the four most common silane SAMs in microfluidics. APTES enables protein/DNA conjugation; OTS and fluorosilane create hydrophobic surfaces for droplet-microfluidics or mold release; MPTMS enables thiol-ene grafting of hydrogels and polymers. Fluorosilane on SU-8 / silicon masters is the standard mold-release for PDMS soft lithography (see baseline recipe).

canonical_name: AZ positive photoresist patterning on glass for HF mask
substrate_material: Borosilicate or soda-lime glass slide; AZ positive photoresist (AZ 4620 or AZ P4620 thick; AZ 1518 thin)
output_artifact: Patterned positive photoresist mask suitable as HF / BHF wet-etch resist for glass microfluidic channels.

steps.parameters: Sonicate in 2% Hellmanex / DI 5 min, DI rinse 3x, IPA, N2 dry. Dehydration bake 200 °C 10 min.
steps.notes: Skip piranha if glass is fresh (not refurbished); piranha attacks soda-lime over time.

steps.parameters: Spin-coat HMDS at 4000 rpm 30 s OR vapor-prime in HMDS oven at 130 °C 5 min.
steps.notes: Critical for AZ resist on glass; without HMDS, resist lifts during HF etch.

steps.parameters: For AZ 4620 (5-10 µm thick mask): spin 2000-3000 rpm 30 s with 5 s ramp. For AZ 1518 (1.5 µm thin): spin 4000 rpm 30 s. Static dispense 2 mL.
steps.notes: AZ 4620 thicker for protective HF etch mask. Soft-bake immediately.

steps.parameters: AZ 4620: hot plate 95-110 °C for 90-180 s. AZ 1518: 95 °C 60 s. Avoid high-temp ramp that causes resist crack.
steps.notes: Drives off solvent; crucial for exposure response.

steps.parameters: AZ 4620 at 5 µm: dose 250-400 mJ/cm² at 365 nm (g+h+i broadband acceptable). AZ 1518: 80-120 mJ/cm².
steps.notes: AZ resists are positive-tone: exposed areas develop away. Use chrome mask of channel pattern (clear field defines etched zones).

steps.parameters: AZ 4620: AZ 400K developer (KOH-based) diluted 1:4 in DI for 60-180 s. AZ 1518: AZ 351 (TMAH-based) developer 30-60 s. Inspect under microscope; under-development leaves resist in exposed zones.
steps.notes: DI rinse 30 s, N2 dry. KOH developer attacks aluminum (etch step compatibility).

steps.action: Hard bake (recommended for HF etch mask)
steps.parameters: 110-120 °C for 30 min on hot plate. Improves adhesion and HF resistance.
steps.notes: Higher hard bake (>130 °C) reflows resist; not desired for sharp patterning.

critical_parameters.target: vapor or spin prime before resist
critical_parameters.failure_at_off_spec: Skipped HMDS: resist lifts in HF etch within minutes.
Under-baked: nitrogen bubbles during exposure (N2-evolution from sensitizer); over-baked: resist no longer photoactive.
Under-exposed: incomplete development. Over-exposed: feature broadening, T-topping.
Under-developed: resist islands in exposed zones. Over-developed: dark-area resist thinning.
Insufficient hard bake: resist undercut by HF; reduced fidelity.

equipment_required.optional_model: OAI 200 / Suss MJB4 / Karl Suss / 365 nm LED panel

equipment_required.notes: For pattern definition; transparency film acceptable for >25 µm features.

validated_outcomes: AZ 4620 mask thickness 5-10 µm supports BHF (6:1) etching of borosilicate glass to depths 30-100 µm with mask intact. Sidewall slope ~75-85° with 5 µm AZ 4620. AZ 1518 supports etch depths up to ~5 µm before mask failure. Feature resolution 2 µm for AZ 1518; 5 µm for AZ 4620.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Resist peels in HF bath; substrate over-etched
failure_modes.corrective_action: Verify HMDS prime fresh; extend hard bake to 30 min at 120 °C; consider thicker resist.
Extend soft bake to drive off solvent; reduce dose ramp rate; use lower-temp soft bake (95 °C not 110 °C).
Slow soft-bake ramp; multiple-step soft bake (65 → 95 °C); reduce thickness to <8 µm if not needed.
Extend develop; verify developer not exhausted (check pH or replace); check exposure dose.

publication_citation: MicroChemicals GmbH. AZ 4620 product datasheet and processing guide.
sources: MicroChemicals technical bulletin: positive photoresist guide
Iliescu et al. 2008 Sensors 8:6210 (glass photolithography for microfluidics)
notes: AZ positive photoresists are the standard for glass-channel HF/BHF wet etching; complementary to SU-8 negative resist used for PDMS masters. AZ 4620 is the workhorse for HF masking; AZ 1518 for thin precision masking (electrode patterning, lift-off). For features <2 µm, use AZ nLOF 2020 (negative tone, lift-off).

canonical_name: KMPR thick-film negative photoresist (SU-8 alternative for 50-200 µm features)
substrate_material: Silicon wafer (or glass) with KMPR negative photoresist
output_artifact: Patterned KMPR features 50-200 µm tall, suitable as PDMS soft-lithography masters or as structural elements; KMPR strips in conventional positive-resist developer (TMAH) — easier removal than SU-8.

steps.parameters: Acetone / IPA / DI rinse, N2 dry. Dehydration bake 200 °C for 15 min on hot plate, cool to RT.
steps.notes: Dehydration eliminates moisture that causes adhesion failure.

steps.parameters: For KMPR 1050 at 50 µm: spin 1500 rpm for 30 s with 5 s ramp at 100 rpm/s. For 100 µm: 800 rpm for 30 s. For 200 µm: dual-coat at 600 rpm with intermediate soft-bake.
steps.notes: KMPR 1050 covers 25-100 µm in single coat per Kayaku datasheet. Static dispense 2-3 mL.

steps.parameters: For 50 µm KMPR: 100 °C for 12 min on hot plate (ramp from 65 °C). For 100 µm: 100 °C for 25 min. For 200 µm: 100 °C for 50 min.
steps.notes: Slow cooldown reduces edge-bead crack risk. KMPR has higher solvent retention than SU-8 — longer bakes.

steps.parameters: For 50 µm KMPR: 365 nm i-line, dose 700-1000 mJ/cm². For 100 µm: 1000-1500 mJ/cm². For 200 µm: 1500-2000 mJ/cm².
steps.notes: KMPR requires higher dose than SU-8 (less photoinitiator; thicker films absorb more).

steps.parameters: For 50 µm: 100 °C 4 min. For 100 µm: 100 °C 6 min. Critical for crosslinking.
steps.notes: Slow cool from PEB to room temp on hot plate to reduce thermal-stress cracking.

steps.parameters: PGMEA (SU-8 developer works) immersion with mild agitation: 4 min for 50 µm, 8 min for 100 µm. IPA rinse 30 s. KMPR also strips in CD-26 (TMAH-based positive-resist developer) — useful for selective removal.
steps.notes: Inspect under microscope; under-development leaves residue.

steps.parameters: 150 °C for 10 min for adhesion improvement.
steps.notes: Skip for fine features (<10 µm) to avoid thermal distortion.

critical_parameters.failure_at_off_spec: Linear thickness deviation.
Under-baked: incomplete solvent removal, surface bubbles. Over-baked: thermal cure that prevents UV crosslinking.
Under-exposed: T-topping, weak features. Over-exposed: feature broadening.
Insufficient PEB: incomplete crosslinking; features wash off in develop.

critical_parameters.target: 4 min for 50 µm / 8 min for 100 µm
critical_parameters.failure_at_off_spec: Under: residual KMPR. Over: feature thinning by ~5%.

equipment_required.notes: Programmable, level, capable of long holds.

equipment_required.optional_model: OAI 200 / Suss / 365 nm LED with collimator

equipment_required.notes: For high resolution; transparency mask acceptable for features >50 µm.

validated_outcomes: Feature aspect ratios 5:1 (e.g., 20 µm features at 100 µm height) reliably achievable. Sidewall verticality 88-92°. Surface roughness <50 nm RMS. Master usability: 100+ PDMS pulls per master with proper silanization. KMPR also used as structural material for MEMS — chemically stable in many solvents.

failure_modes.corrective_action: Slower soft-bake ramp; use edge-bead removal (EBR) solvent immediately after spin; reduce wafer-edge thickness.
Improve adhesion: O2 plasma pre-treat substrate; verify dehydration bake; consider HMDS prime; verify PEB sufficient.
Extend develop time; agitate more vigorously; check developer quality (replace if exhausted).

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Features wider at top than bottom
failure_modes.corrective_action: Reduce UV dose; check substrate reflectivity (may need anti-reflection layer for very thick films).

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: KMPR won't strip cleanly in PGMEA
failure_modes.corrective_action: KMPR is designed to strip in TMAH-based positive-resist stripper (CD-26 or Remover PG); SU-8 stripper Nano Remover PG also works.

publication_citation: Lee H, Kim K, Kim T, Kim J. Fabrication of high aspect ratio polymer microstructures and microlens arrays using ultrathick negative photoresist. J Micromech Microeng 2003; 13:S99-S107.
sources: Kayaku application note: KMPR vs SU-8
Conradie & Moore 2002 J Micromech Microeng 12:368 (KMPR characterization)
del Campo & Greiner 2007 J Micromech Microeng 17:R81 (SU-8/KMPR review)
notes: KMPR is chemically similar to SU-8 (epoxy-novolac chemistry) but designed to be removable in standard developers. Useful when masters need to be stripped from substrates (e.g., for substrate reuse) or when KMPR is used as a structural / sacrificial layer rather than just a master. Not as well-characterized for PDMS soft lithography as SU-8; for new processes use SU-8 unless KMPR-specific properties (strippability) are needed.

canonical_name: Sylgard 527 soft PDMS for cell mechanics chips
substrate_material: Sylgard 527 silicone dielectric gel (Dow), optionally blended with Sylgard 184 for tunable modulus
output_artifact: Soft PDMS layer with elastic modulus 5-200 kPa (vs 1-3 MPa for Sylgard 184), suitable for cell-mechanics studies, traction-force microscopy substrates, and brain/lung tissue-mimetic chambers.

steps.parameters: Sylgard 527 alone (1:1 part A:B): E ~5 kPa. Sylgard 527 + 184 blend: 9:1 (527:184) → ~10 kPa; 1:1 → ~75 kPa; 1:9 → ~500 kPa; pure 184 → 2 MPa.
steps.notes: Modulus values from Palchesko et al. 2012 PLoS ONE; verify with rheometer for critical applications.

steps.parameters: Sylgard 527 part A:B = 1:1 by mass (vs 10:1 for 184). Mix gently 5 min in disposable cup; degas under vacuum 30 min until clear.
steps.notes: 527 is two-part platinum-cured silicone; mix ratio inversion gives different cure stoichiometry — do not blend with 184 mix ratios.

steps.parameters: For intermediate modulus: prepare 527 (1:1) and 184 (10:1) separately; combine in target ratio (e.g., 1:1 by mass); mix gently 5 min; degas 30 min.
steps.notes: Blending shifts modulus continuously; calibration curves available in Palchesko 2012.

steps.parameters: Pour onto silanized SU-8 master to ~1-3 mm thickness. Degas in vacuum desiccator 30 min until bubble-free.
steps.notes: 527 is more viscous than 184; degassing may take longer.

steps.parameters: Pure 527: 65 °C 4 h, OR 100 °C 1 h. Blend: cure at temperature appropriate for 184 fraction (typically 65-80 °C 4 h). Avoid >120 °C — degrades soft 527 modulus.
steps.notes: 527 cures fully at lower temperatures than 184; over-cure risks crosslink density increase that hardens material.

steps.parameters: Demold gently (soft material tears easily). Plasma bond to glass: 18 W, 30 s, contact within 60 s. Bond strength of soft PDMS-glass is reduced (~50% of 184-glass bond) — lower test pressures.
steps.notes: For cell-substrate applications, the soft PDMS doesn't need to seal channels — used as a flat compliant substrate with cells on top.

critical_parameters.failure_at_off_spec: Off-stoichiometry: incomplete cure (sticky surface) or harder-than-spec material.
>120 °C: crosslink density increase, modulus rise; <50 °C: cure incomplete (days).
Modulus calibration shifts non-linearly with blend; verify by rheometry.
Bubbles in soft PDMS are catastrophic for cell mechanics measurements (modulus heterogeneity).
Soft PDMS tears at moderate strain; demolding requires care.

equipment_required.notes: For bonding; lower power than for stiff PDMS.

validated_outcomes: Pure Sylgard 527 (1:1): elastic modulus E = 5-7 kPa (range across literature). 1:1 527:184 blend: E ~75 kPa. 1:9 527:184: E ~500 kPa. Modulus stable over weeks at 4 °C in PBS. Compatible with traction-force microscopy fluorescent bead embedding (1-100 nm beads).

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Surface tacky to touch; PDMS sheet sticks to itself
failure_modes.corrective_action: Verify mix ratio 1:1 (not 10:1); extend cure time; verify 527 cure agent (B) fresh and not frozen/separated.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Macroscopic tear when peeling from master
failure_modes.corrective_action: Fresh fluorosilane on master; thicker bulk PDMS (>2 mm); slower peel rate; cool to RT before demolding.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Rheometer or AFM nano-indentation gives high modulus
failure_modes.corrective_action: Reduce cure temperature; reduce cure time; verify mix ratio by mass (not volume); avoid post-cure thermal cycling.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Soft PDMS peels off glass easily
failure_modes.corrective_action: Use covalent attachment via silane chemistry instead of plasma; or use stiffer 184 thin layer as adhesion intermediate.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Cells round up and don't spread
failure_modes.corrective_action: Coat surface with fibronectin (10 µg/mL, 1 h, 37 °C) or collagen — soft PDMS is more bio-inert than 184.

publication_citation: Palchesko RN, Zhang L, Sun Y, Feinberg AW. Development of polydimethylsiloxane substrates with tunable elastic modulus to study cell mechanobiology in muscle and nerve. PLoS ONE 2012; 7:e51499. DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0051499
sources: Wang et al. 2014 Cell Reports 7:2108 (use of soft PDMS for muscle cell mechanics)
Engler et al. 2006 Cell 126:677 (substrate stiffness & cell fate, motivating soft PDMS use)
notes: Sylgard 527 was originally developed as a dielectric gel for electronics. Its low modulus and biocompatibility have made it a workhorse for cell-mechanics studies. Blending with 184 enables continuous modulus tuning between brain (~0.5 kPa, requires <100% 527) and muscle/bone (~10 kPa to 1 MPa range, blends). For modulus <1 kPa, polyacrylamide gels are preferred (PDMS lower limit ~5 kPa).

canonical_name: Replica molding from electroformed nickel master
substrate_material: Electroformed nickel shim master (commercial fabrication) + PDMS replica
output_artifact: PDMS or thermoplastic chip replicated from Ni shim master; thousands of replications per master vs 100s for SU-8.

steps.parameters: Commercial Ni electroforming services accept SU-8/silicon master (or CAD file for direct laser-write of master). Typical Ni shim: 200-500 µm thick, polished back side. Cost ~$500-3000 per shim.
steps.notes: Vendors: Stratec, microPro GmbH, Optisense, Microfluidic ChipShop; minimum order varies.

steps.parameters: Inspect under stereo microscope for replication fidelity, defects (pits, voids in plating). Measure feature heights with optical profilometer; compare to spec.
steps.notes: Defect rate <1 per cm² acceptable for most applications.

steps.parameters: Sonicate Ni shim in IPA 5 min, dry. Apply fluorosilane release: vapor-deposit trichloro(perfluorooctyl)silane in vacuum desiccator (50-100 µL per chamber) for 1-12 h.
steps.notes: Ni master can be re-silanized many times; fluorosilane is consumed by reaction with surface oxide.

steps.parameters: Mix Sylgard 184 (10:1), degas 30 min, pour onto Ni shim to ~3-5 mm thickness. Degas 15 min more to remove cast bubbles.
steps.notes: For thermoplastic chip via injection molding, Ni shim is mounted in mold tool; PDMS process is identical to SU-8 master replication.

steps.parameters: 65 °C for 4 h on level hot plate. Or 80 °C 2 h. Avoid temperature gradients — Ni conducts heat well, so temperature uniformity is good.
steps.notes: Higher temps (>120 °C) may stress Ni-PDMS adhesion.

steps.parameters: Allow to cool to RT. Peel PDMS from one corner; full release should be smooth. Inspect master for residue.
steps.notes: Ni masters typically release more cleanly than SU-8 masters because Ni is harder; many replications without master degradation.

steps.parameters: Ni masters typically support 1000+ PDMS pulls without re-silanization (vs ~100 for SU-8). Re-silanize when release force notably increases.
steps.notes: Track release force qualitatively; sudden increase indicates need to re-silanize.

critical_parameters.failure_at_off_spec: Defects propagate to every replica; reject master if >5/cm².
Release force grows; eventually PDMS sticks and may damage master.
Off-stoichiometry produces sticky or brittle PDMS.
Higher: faster cure, slight residual stress; lower: incomplete cure.

validated_outcomes: Ni shim feature fidelity: ~1-2 µm offset from SU-8 source master typical; resolution down to 1 µm demonstrated commercially. PDMS replica fidelity: <500 nm dimensional offset from Ni master. Master longevity: 1000-5000+ PDMS pulls per master without measurable degradation.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: PDMS tears or master features pull out
failure_modes.corrective_action: Re-silanize with fresh fluorosilane; verify master surface clean before silanation; check for finger oils.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Sharp corners in design appear rounded in PDMS
failure_modes.corrective_action: Inspect Ni master fidelity (electroforming conditions can round corners); request electroformer use lower current density.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: PDMS surface texture inherits Ni grain pattern
failure_modes.corrective_action: Polish back side of Ni shim if not polished; or request lower-roughness electroforming.
Store in dry environment with oxygen scavenger; clean with mild acid (5% acetic acid) carefully; consider Ni-PTFE composite for long-term storage.

publication_citation: Becker H, Gärtner C. Polymer microfabrication methods for microfluidic analytical applications. Electrophoresis 2000; 21:12-26. DOI 10.1002/(SICI)1522-2683(20000101)21:1<12::AID-ELPS12>3.0.CO;2-7
sources: Heckele & Schomburg 2004 J Micromech Microeng 14:R1 (hot embossing review)
notes: Ni electroforming is the standard route from prototype (SU-8) to high-volume injection-molded chip. Workflow: SU-8 master → Ni shim (electroform) → injection-molding tool → thermoplastic chips. For research labs, Ni shim can substitute SU-8 master directly for PDMS replication when high replication count or feature durability matters. Total cost: ~$500-3000 per shim, vs ~$50-200 per SU-8 master, but amortized over 1000+ replications.

canonical_name: Paper microfluidics via SU-8 photoresist patterning on chromatography paper
substrate_material: Whatman chromatography paper (No. 1 or No. 4) impregnated with SU-8 negative photoresist
output_artifact: Paper microfluidic chip with hydrophobic SU-8 barriers defining channels and detection zones; resolution <200 µm features.

steps.parameters: Cut Whatman No. 1 (180 µm thick, 11 µm pore) or No. 4 (210 µm thick, 25 µm pore) chromatography paper to ~7.5 cm x 7.5 cm sheets.
steps.notes: Paper grade affects wicking speed: No. 4 wicks faster, gives lower resolution; No. 1 is the workhorse.

steps.parameters: Pour SU-8 2010 (or 3010 — newer formulation) onto paper to fully impregnate. Excess wicks through; soak 5 min until fully saturated. Place on aluminum foil.
steps.notes: Use SU-8 thinned 1:1 with cyclopentanone for No. 4 paper (faster penetration); full-strength for No. 1.

steps.parameters: Spin paper with SU-8 at 2000 rpm for 30 s on photoresist spinner with vacuum chuck (paper held by Al-foil backing or low-vacuum chuck).
steps.notes: Removes surface excess; SU-8 remains absorbed in fibers.

steps.parameters: Bake on hot plate 95 °C for 5-10 min. Drives off solvent. Paper visibly stiffens but should remain flexible.
steps.notes: Cyclopentanone evaporates upward; bake aluminum side down.

steps.parameters: Place photomask (transparency film acceptable for >100 µm features; chrome for <100 µm). Expose 365 nm UV at dose 1000-2000 mJ/cm² (higher than for thin-film SU-8 due to absorption by paper).
steps.notes: Dose 2-3x higher than for solid SU-8 of equivalent thickness due to absorption by cellulose.

steps.parameters: 95 °C 5 min. Crosslinks exposed SU-8.
steps.notes: Slow cool to room temp.

steps.parameters: Immerse in PGMEA (SU-8 developer) 5 min with mild agitation. Then 60 s in IPA. Air-dry; do not blow with N2 (paper deforms).
steps.notes: Unexposed SU-8 in channel zones washes out, leaving cellulose channels. Exposed barriers retain crosslinked SU-8.

steps.parameters: Drop colored aqueous solution (food dye in water) on inlet; verify wicking confined to designed channels. Measure barrier resolution (feature width vs design).
steps.notes: Resolution typical 200-500 µm with transparency mask; <200 µm with chrome mask.

critical_parameters.failure_at_off_spec: Wrong grade affects wicking speed and barrier resolution.

critical_parameters.target: full saturation, surface excess removed by spin
critical_parameters.failure_at_off_spec: Under-impregnation: incomplete barriers (channel leakage). Over-saturation: excess SU-8 on surface that doesn't develop cleanly.
Insufficient: trapped solvent → bubbles during exposure. Over-baked: paper brittles.
Too low: weak barriers, dye leaks. Too high: barriers spread laterally beyond mask features.
Insufficient: SU-8 residue in channels blocks wicking. Excessive: SU-8 barriers thin.

equipment_required.instrument_class: spin coater (vacuum chuck adapted for paper)
equipment_required.notes: Or skip spin step and let excess soak; manual blot acceptable.

equipment_required.instrument_class: UV mask aligner or LED panel

validated_outcomes: Channel resolution 200 µm typical with transparency mask; <100 µm demonstrated with chrome mask. Barrier hydrophobicity sufficient to confine aqueous flow at lateral hydrostatic pressures up to ~5 cm H2O. Multi-zone tests with 3-5 zones routine. Cost per chip ~$0.10 in materials.

failure_modes.corrective_action: Verify SU-8 fully impregnated paper; increase exposure dose; verify post-exposure bake done; check for cracks in barriers from over-baking.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Aqueous sample doesn't enter channel after deposition
failure_modes.corrective_action: Develop time too short — extend PGMEA bath; verify paper not too dry (re-hydrate by wicking water through).
Reduce bake temperatures; do not blow paper with N2 (use ambient drying).
Use chrome mask instead of transparency; reduce mask-to-paper gap (vacuum contact ideal); reduce dose.

publication_citation: Martinez AW, Phillips ST, Butte MJ, Whitesides GM. Patterned paper as a platform for inexpensive, low-volume, portable bioassays. Angew Chem Int Ed 2007; 46:1318-1320. DOI 10.1002/anie.200603817
sources: Martinez et al. 2007 Angew Chem (foundational paper µPAD)
Martinez et al. 2008 Anal Chem 80:3699 (SU-8 photolithography on paper)
Carrilho et al. 2009 Anal Chem 81:7091 (wax printing comparison)
notes: SU-8 photolithography gives the highest resolution among paper-microfluidics patterning techniques but requires UV exposure equipment. Wax printing (separate recipe) is faster and cheaper for rapid prototyping; SU-8 is preferred for sub-200 µm feature work. Limitation: SU-8 is not biodegradable, reducing the biodegradability advantage of paper substrates.

canonical_name: CO2 laser cutting of PDMS sheets for open-channel chips

canonical_name: GelMA (gelatin methacrylate) photopolymerization in microfluidic chambers
substrate_material: Pre-fabricated PDMS-glass microfluidic chip with chamber for GelMA + cells

steps.parameters: Synthesize GelMA from Type A gelatin + methacrylic anhydride (1.25 mL per g gelatin) in PBS at 50 °C for 1-3 h, then dialyze 5 days against DI water (12-14 kDa MWCO), lyophilize. Or purchase commercially: Allevi GelMA, CELLINK Bio-X GelMA, Advanced Biomatrix PhotoGel.
steps.duration: 1 week synthesis or 5 min reconstitution from purchased
steps.notes: Degree of methacrylation (DoM) typically 60-90%; affects crosslink density and stiffness. NMR for verification.

steps.parameters: Dissolve GelMA in PBS or cell media at 5-15% w/v. Warm to 37 °C for 30 min until fully dissolved. Add photoinitiator: LAP at 0.1-0.5% w/v (visible 405 nm) or Irgacure 2959 at 0.1-0.5% (UV 365 nm).
steps.notes: GelMA solubility limit ~20% w/v; above this, viscosity becomes problematic. LAP preferred for cell viability.

steps.parameters: Resuspend cells in pre-warmed GelMA solution at 1-10 million cells/mL. Mix gently to avoid bubbles.
steps.notes: Pipette tips wide-bore to reduce shear on cells.

steps.parameters: Use syringe pump or pipette to fill GelMA into pre-equilibrated microchamber at 37 °C (chip on heated stage). Fill rate 1-10 µL/min depending on geometry.
steps.notes: GelMA gels at <30 °C; keep chip warm during fill or pre-cool only the channel zones to confine gel.

steps.parameters: Expose 405 nm at 5-15 mW/cm² for 15-60 s (with LAP) for cell viability. Or 365 nm at 5-10 mW/cm² for 30-90 s (with Irgacure 2959).
steps.notes: Lower dose preserves cell viability but may give weaker gel. Calibrate dose per use case (typically 0.5-2 J/cm²).

steps.parameters: Flush with warm PBS or media to remove uncrosslinked GelMA and photoinitiator. Continue media perfusion at 0.1-1 µL/min for cell culture. Maintain 37 °C, 5% CO2.
steps.notes: Uncrosslinked GelMA at 37 °C remains liquid; thorough flush essential.

canonical_name: Alginate-CaCl2 ionic crosslinking for cell encapsulation in droplet microfluidics
substrate_material: Alginate aqueous phase + oil continuous phase + CaCl2 crosslinking source (in oil phase or in collection bath)
output_artifact: Monodisperse Ca-alginate hydrogel microbeads (typically 50-200 µm diameter) with optional cell encapsulation; gentle, reagent-free crosslinking compatible with most cell types.

steps.parameters: Dissolve sodium alginate (low or medium viscosity, MW 100-500 kDa) at 1-3% w/v in PBS or DI. Stir 2-4 h until fully dissolved. Filter 0.45 µm. Sterilize via filter (autoclaving degrades).
steps.notes: High-G alginate (≥50% guluronate) gels stronger with Ca²⁺ than high-M alginate. Sigma medium-viscosity is workhorse.

steps.parameters: Method A (delayed): mineral oil + 2% Span 80 surfactant; CaCl2 in collection bath only. Method B (in-line): mineral oil + 2% Span 80 + 0.1-0.5% CaCl2 dissolved in non-ionic surfactant (e.g., HFE-7500 + Pico-Surf with Ca2+ chelate that releases on UV/pH).
steps.notes: Method A is simpler; Method B gives faster gelation but more complex chemistry.

steps.parameters: Resuspend cells in alginate solution at 1-50 million cells/mL. Use wide-bore pipette tips. Alginate is shear-thinning; gentle mixing.
steps.notes: Cells in alginate stable at 4 °C up to 1 h.

steps.parameters: Use flow-focusing or T-junction device. Typical flow rates: alginate 0.5-2 µL/min, oil 5-20 µL/min. Droplet size 50-200 µm by aqueous:oil ratio.
steps.notes: Higher alginate concentration → higher viscosity → larger droplets at same flow ratio.

steps.parameters: Collect droplets in CaCl2 bath: 100-500 mM CaCl2 in PBS. Stir gently 5-10 min. Wash 3x in PBS to remove excess Ca²⁺.
steps.notes: Simplest method; gel forms within seconds of contact with bath.

steps.parameters: For UV-released calcium: expose collected emulsion to 365 nm UV at 50-100 mJ/cm² to release Ca2+. For pH-shift: add acetic acid downstream to lower pH and release calcium from EDTA chelate.
steps.notes: More precise control but requires additional chip features and chemistry.

steps.parameters: De-emulsify with 20% perfluorooctanol in HFE-7500 (for fluorinated oil) or by centrifugation (for mineral oil). Wash beads 3x in PBS.
steps.notes: For cell-laden beads, gentle centrifugation (200 g, 1 min) preserves viability.

critical_parameters.failure_at_off_spec: <0.5%: gel too weak. >5%: viscosity too high to inject in droplet device.
<50 mM: gel under-crosslinked. >1000 mM: osmotic shock to cells.
Higher G gives stiffer gel; lower G gives softer/more permeable.
High CV indicates flow instability; check syringe pumps and chip.
Insufficient: droplets coalesce. Excessive: micelles deplete oil-phase Ca2+.

equipment_required.notes: Custom or commercial; channel dimensions 50-200 µm.

validated_outcomes: Bead diameter 50-200 µm with <5% CV achievable via flow-focusing. Bead modulus 5-50 kPa depending on alginate and Ca2+ concentrations. Cell viability (HEK293, hMSCs, primary islets) >90% with Method A; lower with UV-Ca2+ release. Bead stability: stable in cell media for >1 week; degrades in citrate or EDTA (cell release).

failure_modes.corrective_action: Increase surfactant; reduce dispersed-phase flow rate; ensure CaCl2 bath agitated to prevent aggregation.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Dead cells visible in or near beads
failure_modes.corrective_action: Reduce CaCl2 to 100 mM; reduce wash duration; use cell-friendly surfactant; check for shear damage at junction.

failure_modes.diagnostic_signature: Beads disappear over hours in media
failure_modes.corrective_action: Avoid phosphate-rich buffers (Ca2+ phosphate competes with alginate); wash thoroughly to remove un-crosslinked alginate; consider barium-alginate (Ba2+ instead of Ca2+) for more stable beads.

steps.parameters: vapor-phase perfluorosilane in vacuum desiccator 1 h
Sylgard 184 10:1, degas, pour onto PLA mold, cure 65 °C × 60 min
peel PDMS from PLA, plasma-bond to glass

critical_parameters.failure_at_off_spec: coarse layers transfer to chip
PDMS sticks to PLA on peel

equipment_required.instrument_class: FDM 3D printer with 0.4 mm or finer nozzle

validated_outcome: PDMS chips with channel widths >200 µm; useful for prototyping where SU-8 photolithography unavailable.

failure_modes.mode: Layer lines visible in PDMS chip
failure_modes.corrective_action: smooth PLA before casting; or use SLA-printed mold
cure PDMS at 50 °C (PLA Tg ~60 °C); use longer cure time

publication_citation: Comina et al. 2014 Lab Chip 14 (FDM molds for PDMS); Walczak & Adamski 2015
notes: PLA not biocompatible for cell culture; use only as sacrificial mold material. PDMS chip itself is biocompatible.
